w: All-day Lower East Side kopi shop for Malaysian-Singaporean classics, including a tender poached Hainanese chicken rice with fragrant ginger-oiled rice.
Sunset Park Malaysian counter built around one dish: silky poached Hainanese chicken over oiled rice with chili and ginger-scallion sauces.
Greenpoint Taiwanese hit from the 886 team, an Infatuation favorite whose menu includes a delicate poached Hainanese chicken alongside the viral BDSM chicken.
Tiny cash-only Elmhurst specialist perfecting Thai-style khao man kai, silky poached Hainanese chicken over schmaltz rice with a punchy chili-soybean sauce.
Chinatown Thai chicken-and-rice shop serving a cheap, tender Thai-style Hainanese chicken rice bowl, most items under ten dollars.
Family-run Hong Kong-style Chinatown spot widely called the best wonton noodle soup around, shrimp-packed wontons in a clean, light broth.
No-frills hole-in-the-wall on Doyers Street famous for the pork wonton hand-pulled noodle soup, noodles stretched fresh to order.
Bayard Street Shanghainese stalwart since 1982 whose signature hot and spicy wontons come drenched in peanut sauce and chili oil.
Cash-only Eldridge Street counter for Lanzhou hand-pulled noodles, with a Fujianese wonton soup you can pair with the fresh-stretched noodles.
Cantonese wonton specialist the Infatuation calls one of NYC's best bowls, dumpling-trio lo mein of pork, shrimp and watercress wontons over springy egg noodles.
Flushing Hong Kong-style noodle house known for supersized shrimp wontons and dace fishballs over thin egg noodles in a rich broth.
